title: Jacobi-Zariski sequence of a tower of fields is exact on the left
statement: Let $K\subseteq L\subseteq M$ be field extensions. For a ring map $R\to S$ let $H_1(L_{S/R})$ be the first homology of the naive cotangent complex $\mathrm{NL}_{S/R}$ of the canonical presentation $R[S]\to S$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], and $\Omega_{S/R}$ the module of K\"ahler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Let $a:H_1(L_{L/K})\otimes_LM\to H_1(L_{M/K})$ be the $M$-linear map $h\otimes c\mapsto c\cdot\iota_*(h)$, where $\iota_*:H_1(L_{L/K})\to H_1(L_{M/K})$ is induced by the morphism of presentations $K[L]\to K[M]$, $[l]\mapsto[l]$, over the square $K=K$, $L\subseteq M$ [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality]. Then the sequence of $M$-vector spaces $$0\to H_1(L_{L/K})\otimes_LM\xrightarrow{a}H_1(L_{M/K})\xrightarrow{v}H_1(L_{M/L})\xrightarrow{\partial}\Omega_{L/K}\otimes_LM\xrightarrow{w}\Omega_{M/K}\xrightarrow{z}\Omega_{M/L}\to0,$$ with $v,\partial,w,z$ the maps of the Jacobi-Zariski sequence for $K\to L\to M$ [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-homology-sequence], is exact. In particular $a$ is injective.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07E2 (lemma-transitivity-gamma, line 8599); its proof combines More on Algebra Lemma Tag 07D5 (lemma-transitive-colimit-lci-at-end) with Algebra Lemma Tag 07BV (lemma-colimit-syntomic): every field extension of K is a filtered colimit of global complete intersections over K. Tags verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags.

proof.text: *The Jacobi-Zariski sequence.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-homology-sequence] to $A=K$, $B=L$, $C=M$ with $\varphi:L\to M$ the inclusion. It gives the $M$-linear maps $u_M:H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{L/K}\otimes_LM)\to H_1(L_{M/K})$, $v$, $\partial$, $w$, $z$ and the exact sequence $H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{L/K}\otimes_LM)\xrightarrow{u_M}H_1(L_{M/K})\xrightarrow{v}H_1(L_{M/L})\xrightarrow{\partial}M\otimes_L\Omega_{L/K}\xrightarrow{w}\Omega_{M/K}\xrightarrow{z}\Omega_{M/L}\to0$. Transporting $\partial$ and $w$ along the isomorphism $M\otimes_L\Omega_{L/K}\cong\Omega_{L/K}\otimes_LM$, $c\otimes\omega\mapsto\omega\otimes c$, this is exactness of the sequence of the statement at $H_1(L_{M/L})$, $\Omega_{L/K}\otimes_LM$, $\Omega_{M/K}$ and $\Omega_{M/L}$. It remains to show exactness at $H_1(L_{M/K})$ and injectivity of $a$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07D4 (lemma-transitive-lci-at-end, lines 8459-8492): the six-term sequence of Algebra Lemma 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), whose completion on the left is the content of 07D4/07D5 used in the proof of Lemma 07E2 (line 8615)

proof.text: *Over the field $L$ the Tor terms vanish.* Let $C$ be any $L$-algebra (it will be $M$ or an $L$-subalgebra of $M$). The $L$-module $\Omega_{L/K}$ is free [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-free], so $F_0=\Omega_{L/K}$, $F_i=0$ for $i\ge1$, with the identity $F_0\to\Omega_{L/K}$, is a free resolution, and by [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules] $\operatorname{Tor}^L_i(\Omega_{L/K},C)$ is the $i$-th homology of $\cdots\to0\to F_0\otimes_LC\to0$, which is $0$ for $i\ge1$. Hence, by the last clause of [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-homology-sequence] for $K\to L\to C$, the $C$-linear map $\theta_C:H_1(L_{L/K})\otimes_LC\to H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{L/K}\otimes_LC)$, $h\otimes c\mapsto h\otimes c$, is an isomorphism.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), its statement on H_1(NL_{B/A} tensor C) under Tor vanishing (lines 35411-35485); the flatness of every module over a field is implicit in the proof of More on Algebra 07E2 (line 8615)

proof.text: *The map $a$ is $u$ composed with $\theta$.* For an $L$-subalgebra $C\subseteq M$ (including $C=M$) let $a_C:H_1(L_{L/K})\otimes_LC\to H_1(L_{C/K})$, $h\otimes c\mapsto c\cdot\iota^C_*(h)$, where $\iota^C_*$ is induced by the morphism of presentations $\iota^C:K[L]\to K[C]$, $[l]\mapsto[l]$, over the square $K=K$, $L\subseteq C$ [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality]; so $a_M=a$. By that node, $\iota^C_*(g\bmod I_{L/K}^2)=\iota^C(g)\bmod I_{C/K}^2$ for $g\in I_{L/K}$ with class in $H_1(L_{L/K})$, and $\iota^C$ is the map $\varphi_\sharp$ of [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-homology-sequence] (a) for $K\to L\to C$. Hence $u_C(\theta_C((g\bmod I_{L/K}^2)\otimes c))=c\cdot(\iota^C(g)\bmod I_{C/K}^2)=a_C((g\bmod I_{L/K}^2)\otimes c)$, so $a_C=u_C\circ\theta_C$ on generators and hence everywhere. Since $\theta_C$ is bijective (step 2), $a_C$ is injective if and only if $u_C$ is, and $\operatorname{im}a_C=\operatorname{im}u_C$. For $C=M$: $\operatorname{im}a=\operatorname{im}u_M=\ker v$ by step 1, which is exactness at $H_1(L_{M/K})$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07E2 (lemma-transitivity-gamma, line 8599): the left map of its sequence is the map H_1(NL_{B/A} tensor C) -> H_1(L_{C/A}) of Lemma 07D4 (line 8484) after the identification of step 2

proof.text: *Finite stages.* Let $C\subseteq M$ be an $L$-subalgebra for which there are $n,c\ge0$, a regular sequence $f_1,\dots,f_c$ in $L[Y_1,\dots,Y_n]$ and an isomorphism of $L$-algebras $L[Y_1,\dots,Y_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)\cong C$. Composing the quotient map with this isomorphism gives a surjective $L$-algebra map $\beta:L[Y_1,\dots,Y_n]\to C$ with kernel $(f_1,\dots,f_c)$, so [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-regular-sequence-left-injective] applies to $K\to L\to C$ and $u_C$ is injective (its $u$ is the $u_C$ of step 3, defined by the same formula). By step 3, $a_C:H_1(L_{L/K})\otimes_LC\to H_1(L_{C/K})$ is injective.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07D5 (lemma-transitive-colimit-lci-at-end, line 8508): Lemma 07D4 applied at each stage of the colimit (proof, lines 8516-8521)

proof.text: *Passage to $M$.* Let $x\in H_1(L_{L/K})\otimes_LM$ with $a(x)=0$. Write $x=\sum_{j=1}^rh_j\otimes m_j$ with $m_j\in M$ and $h_j=g_j\bmod I_{L/K}^2$, $g_j\in I_{L/K}\subseteq K[L]$. In $I_{M/K}/I_{M/K}^2$ (where $c\in M$ acts as multiplication by $[c]$) we have $a(x)=G\bmod I_{M/K}^2$ with $G=\sum_j[m_j]\,\iota^M(g_j)\in I_{M/K}$, so $a(x)=0$ means $G=\sum_{k=1}^tp_kq_k$ for some $p_k,q_k\in I_{M/K}$. Let $E\subseteq M$ be the finite set consisting of $m_1,\dots,m_r$ and of all $s\in M$ such that the variable $[s]$ occurs in one of $p_1,q_1,\dots,p_t,q_t$. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-complete-intersection-subalgebras] for the field extension $M/L$ there are a regular sequence $f_1,\dots,f_c$ in $L[Y_1,\dots,Y_n]$ and an injective $L$-algebra map $L[Y_1,\dots,Y_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)\to M$ whose image $C$ contains $E$; $C$ is an $L$-subalgebra of $M$ as in step 4, and $L\subseteq C$. For the subset $C\subseteq M$ the polynomial ring $K[C]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] is the subring of $K[M]$ of polynomials in the variables $[s]$, $s\in C$; the canonical presentation $\gamma_C:K[C]\to C$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] is the restriction of $\gamma_M:K[M]\to M$, and $C\to M$ is injective, so $I_{C/K}=I_{M/K}\cap K[C]$. Also $\iota^M$ is $\iota^C$ followed by $K[C]\subseteq K[M]$. Hence $p_k,q_k\in K[C]\cap I_{M/K}=I_{C/K}$, $G=\sum_j[m_j]\iota^C(g_j)\in I_{C/K}^2$, and for $x_C=\sum_jh_j\otimes m_j\in H_1(L_{L/K})\otimes_LC$ we get $a_C(x_C)=G\bmod I_{C/K}^2=0$. By step 4, $x_C=0$, so $x$, the image of $x_C$ under $\mathrm{id}\otimes(C\subseteq M):H_1(L_{L/K})\otimes_LC\to H_1(L_{L/K})\otimes_LM$, is $0$. So $a$ is injective, and with steps 1 and 3 the whole sequence is exact.
